To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have calculated the contributions from radiation in a finite-volume medium to the medium-induced broadening of high energy quarks and gluons, which includes both the double-log correction and the LPM effect, and that the parametrically large corrections from radiation to the broadening are expected in perturbative high energy QCD.
we have calculated the p⊥-brodening of a high energy particle in a medium in the soft gluonic approximation and that we have found a parametrically significant contribution from the LPM-effect.

we found a new parametrically large contribution to the p⊥- broadening of high energy quarks and gluons in a QCD medium, which originates from the interference between the multiple scattering and the medium-induced radiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the medium-induced gluon radiation from the high energy parton in the finite-volume QCD matter.
the p⊥-distribution of high energy parton associated with the LMP effect in QCD medium.
the following questions: (1) How do the LPM effect and the finite-volume effect affect the p⊥-spectrum of the radiated gluon?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in a finite-volume medium, the LPM effect leads to a significant modification of the medium-induced parton p⊥-diffusion, which should be taken into account when studying high energy parton energy loss in a QCD medium.
the LPM effect is important in the p⊥-spectrum for high energy partons in a finite-volume medium.
the medium-induced p ⊥ broadening is parametrically large in a QCD medium, and that it is not suppressed by the LPM effect, but rather it is enhanced by the LPM logarithm, in a finite-volume medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medium-induced p ⊥-broadenings are parametrically enhanced compared to those from multiple elastic scatterings.
the p⊥-distribution for high energy partons in a QCD medium can be well described by a Gaussian function, which can be parametrized by the mean square of the transverse momentum broadening.
the medium-induced p ⊥-broadenings of a high energy quark or gluon are parametrically the largest among the medium-modifications of a high energy particle propagating through a QCD medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a medium of finite length L, the LPM effect is not a small effect.
the LPM effect is a universal phenomenon in QCD and should be taken into account in any calculation of medium-induced p⊤-broadening.
the LPM effect is important for p⊥- broadening in a finite volume medium, even though it has no contribution to the medium-induced energy loss.
